key_insight: Sparse noisy tumor-growth data can produce convincing fits and explanations while still yielding the wrong governing law, so law discovery must be judged beyond prediction accuracy.
engineering_relevance: For scientific modeling workflows, the study shows that coefficient refitting and model ranking should be validated against mathematical correctness, not just curve-fit quality.
method: Symbolic regression generates candidate growth laws from sparse data.
Candidates are filtered by mathematical admissibility and then coefficient-refit using either physics-informed neural networks or nonlinear least squares.
An LLM-based ranking step is compared against selection by training error.
evidence_signal: Using synthetic Gompertz data, dense noiseless data recover the true family, while sparse noisy sampling often selects alternative forms; nonlinear least squares usually lowers growth-law error, but PINN refitting often increases it.
watch_item: LLM rankings and high-quality trajectory fits do not guarantee correct law recovery, so downstream selection criteria can be misleading.
paper_title: AI-Assisted Tumor-Growth Law Discovery from Sparse Data: Refitting and LLM-Based Ranking
